newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to spend $160 mln on fuel oil imports.
newsitem.headline: Romania to spend $160 mln on fuel oil imports.

text.p: Romania's Renel RA electricity authority will spend $160 million to import fuel oil for its power plants in order to prevent a new energy crisis over the coming winter months, a company official said.
"We are working now on the last arrangements with two banks to get the $160 million (loan), which is guaranteed by the government," a senior Renel official said.
"Fuel oil imports might start by next week. They can cover the needs of our thermal power plants for quite a long time," said the official, who asked not to be identified.
He declined to name the companies involved in the import operation.
Western oil dealers said they expected Romania to buy around 500,000 tonnes of high sulphur fuel oil over the next month.
At current prices this volume would cost about $65 million.
Bucharest also guaranteed a $200 million loan for crude imports by the state-run Romanian Oil Company over the next months.

The imports are part of moves by Renel and the government to avoid a repeat of the energy crisis which hit the country last winter. An acute shortage of hard currency to pay for fuel imports forced Renel to cut power supplies to industry in January-March.
In August, state secretary Lucian Motiu said Romania would import annually some 10 million tonnes of crude, 4.0 million tonnes of fuel oil and 7.0 billion cubic metres of gas.
Romania annually produces around 6.6 million tonnes of crude and some 20 billion cubic metres of gas. -- Adrian Dascalu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
